ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Cities $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, and $E$ are connected by roads $\widetilde{AB}$, $\widetilde{AD}$, $\widetilde{AE}$, $\widetilde{BC}$, $\widetilde{BD}$, $\widetilde{CD}$, $\widetilde{DE}$. How many different routes are there from $A$ to $B$ that use each road exactly once? (Such a route will necessarily visit cities more than once.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows five cities A, B, C, D, and E connected by the roads AB, AD, AE, BC, BD, CD, and DE, matching the problem statement. Following the assigned compression method: Cities C and E both have degree 2. Since C is incident only to BC and CD, any route using every road exactly once must pass through C as the single chain B-C-D. Similarly, since E is incident only to AE and DE, the route must pass through E as the single chain A-E-D. So we replace the original graph by a multigraph on A, B, and D with five distinct links: one A-B link, two A-D links, and two B-D links. We now count Euler trails from A to B in this compressed multigraph. Ignoring labels of the two parallel A-D links and the two parallel B-D links, the valid link-type sequences are: 1. AB, BD, AD, AD, BD 2. AD, AD, AB, BD, BD 3. AD, BD, AB, AD, BD 4. AD, BD, BD, AD, AB For each valid type sequence, the two A-D links can be assigned in 2 ways, and the two B-D links can be assigned in 2 ways. Thus each type sequence gives 2 × 2 = 4 distinct routes. Therefore the total number of routes is 4 × 4 = 16.

method.method_draft: Compress the graph using the degree-2 cities C and E. Read the roads as AB, AD, AE, BC, BD, CD, DE. Since C has only BC and CD, any route using both exactly once must pass through C as a single B-D chain. Since E has only AE and DE, it must pass through E as a single A-D chain. Thus replace the original graph by a 3-city multigraph on A, B, D with five distinct links: one A-B link, two A-D links, and two B-D links. Now count Euler trails from A to B in this multigraph. Ignoring the labels of the parallel links first, the valid link-type sequences are: AB,BD,AD,AD,BD; AD,AD,AB,BD,BD; AD,BD,AB,AD,BD; AD,BD,BD,AD,AB. For each sequence, the two A-D links can be ordered in 2 ways and the two B-D links can be ordered in 2 ways, giving 4 routes per sequence. Total = 4 × 4 = 16.
